title: Attention runtime hypothesis sprint 04 - observations
content:
Purpose:
This sprint (04) focused on a short, targeted investigation of an intermittent tail-latency cliff observed in the hosted inference fleet when serving medium-length responses (256-1024 tokens) under mixed-batch traffic. The goal was to exercise kernel-selection boundaries between FlashAttention-family kernels, paged attention, and fused-ops paths to surface decision thresholds and a reproducible repro for follow-up fixes.

Background/context (quick):
- Multiple customer incidents in Oct showed p95 spikes to 450ms from a baseline ~120ms for the same model and region.
- Hypothesis space: kernel switch thrash; KV cache eviction/prefetch mismatch; prefetch gating disabled for some runs; register pressure causing fallback into non-vectorized path.
- This doc is an experiment log + rough conclusions and next steps. Not a polished playbook yet.

Environment and hardware:
- Cluster: dedicated staging pool (eu-west-1-dedicated-8gpu, A100-40GB equivalence)
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@main (commit 9d3a2f7) + kernel-bench harness PR #789
- Models: rwd/llama-extended-7b (decoder-only, 8 heads, 4096 context), quant: int8 fallback enabled
- Workloads: scripted generator with Poisson arrivals, mixture: 40% short (<=64), 40% mid (256-512), 20% long (1024-2048)
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (inf start->end), kernel choice trace, GPU occupancy, shared-memory stalls, KV cache hit/evict log, ctx-seq length, batch size.

Experiment design (what we toggled):
- Kernel selector thresholds: switch_point_seqlen = {128, 256, 384, 512}
- Batch coalescer window: {4ms, 8ms, 16ms}
- Prefetch policy: aggressive / conservative / off
- Kernel variants tested: FlashAttention2 (FA2), FlashPaged (FP), FusedOps (FO), TiledFallback (TF)
- Warmup: cold start (empty KV cache) vs warmed (preload with 50 warm requests)
- Repetition: 10 runs per config, 5 minutes each, collect p50/p95/p99 and kernel-switch histograms

Quick repro steps (dev scratch):
- start harness: ./bench/run_mixed_workload.sh --model rwd/llama-extended-7b --arrival=poisson --mix=40-40-20 --duration=300 
- enable tracing: export RUNTIME_TRACE_KERNEL=1; tail -f /tmp/kernel-trace.log
- change selector: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/selector -d '{"switch_point_seqlen":256}'

Observations (raw):
1) Repro case: with selector switch_point_seqlen=256 and coalescer=8ms, p95 jumps to 380ms in the mid workload runs; reproduced in 7/10 attempts.
2) Kernel histogram for a spike window shows high fraction of requests flipping between FA2 and FP across the batch: about 30% FA2, 60% FP, 10% TF for same seqlen=300 window.
3) GPU occupancy during spikes drops ~12% and shared-memory stall counters increase markedly => suggests switching to FP produces extra mem copies/paging behavior.
4) Warmed KV cache reduces amplitude of spikes by ~40% on average but does not eliminate them; suggests cache warming mitigates but not root cause.
5) Extremely small batches (batch size 1-2) see increased jitter when kernel selector threshold moves near the median seqlen of the workload.
6) Prefetch aggressive reduces p95 spikes in many configs but increases GPU memory transient pressure leading to occasional OOMs in stress runs.
7) FusedOps path shows best stable p50 but in mixed traffic its internal heuristic to serialize some ops leads to larger p99 when batch mixing occurs.

Representative numeric snapshot (median of runs, pick a typical run):
- Config: switch_point_seqlen=256, coalescer=8ms, prefetch=conservative, warmup=none
  p50: 98ms, p95: 372ms, p99: 622ms, mean GPU occupancy: 67%
- Same config but warmed KV:
  p50: 95ms, p95: 224ms, p99: 412ms, mean GPU occupancy: 73%
- switch_point_seqlen=512, coalescer=8ms:
  p50: 105ms, p95: 168ms, p99: 290ms -> fewer switches to FP, more consistent FA2 runs.

Interpretation / hypotheses refined:
- Kernel selection boundary around 256 tokens seems to sit in a high-variance region when traffic mixes short and mid sequences. Selector instability (oscillation) can cause per-request kernel writes/reads that increase shared-memory stalls and drop occupancy.
- FlashPaged (FP) path appears to allocate transient page buffers or perform additional staging that inflates latency, especially when requests in a batch are heterogeneous (different seqlen causing per-request code paths).
- KV cache warmup reduces the page/fallback pressure because cache hits avoid certain prefetch branches; there's a partial mitigation but not sufficient alone.
- Aggressive prefetch masks the symptom at cost of memory pressure; not safe for multi-tenant/dedicated with limited memory headroom.

Actionable mitigations tested (short-term):
- Move selector boundary to 384-512 for production models that show mixed-mid workloads (immediately reduces p95 at cost of slightly higher p50 for some cases).
- Add lightweight priming phase for new workers: run 50 small warm requests pinned to common seqlen buckets before marking node Ready. This reduced repro rate from 70%->25% in staging tests.
- Add hysteresis to kernel selector: require two consecutive candidate decisions before switching kernel for a batch ID. This eliminated the flip-flop pattern in synthetic tests.

Decisions for next cycle (doR):
- Ship selector hysteresis as default for hosted API for next deploy (behind flag RUNTIME_SELECTOR_HYSTERESIS=2) — low risk, immediate benefit.
- Defer aggressive prefetch as a prod-wide option; instead provide a per-customer toggle behind Dedicated plan until we can bound RAM cost.
- Run long-duration soak tests (24h) on a subset of dedicated nodes with selector set to 512 to measure steady-state throughput and memory tail behavior.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why exactly does FP cause shared-memory stall growth? (need microtrace of kernel internals and memory copy paths)
- Is there a register-pressure threshold (model-specific) that deterministically forces FA2->TF? Need to correlate with per-layer register usage reports from the compiler.
- Are there model-architecture features (rotary vs cos/kv layout) that bias selection? Quick cross-check with another model family recommended.

Notes-to-self / friction log:
- Repro not 100% deterministic; seeding the harness reduces flakiness but real traffic still shows non-determinism.
- Need to add per-request kernel decision id in traces to join to GPU perf counters offline.
- Some profiling hooks added in PR #789 are noisy; consider sampling at 1/10th rate for production telemetry.

Short checklist (immediate):
- [x] Add selector hysteresis flag and test in staging (Marco)
- [x] Implement warm priming bootstrap in worker init (Aisha)
- [ ] Add microtrace instrumentation around FlashPaged allocation points (Jordan)
- [ ] Schedule 24h soak on dedicated subset (Emily)
- [ ] Create follow-up Jira with kernel team to inspect register usage data (INF-2240)
